transcript.text: Morning, everyone. I wanted to kick off our delivery review. As it stands, we've got a 55-minute picture with the draft title card and end credits, and the delivery folder currently has a stereo master, optional subtitle files, and a generic principal-credit block. Before I can lock the episode package and we send it to the streaming distributor, we need sign-off from standards, business affairs, and accessibility. Let's start working through each of those areas.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something critical before we go any further. I reviewed the distributor's regional standards memo this morning, and it specifies that this episode must be delivered at exactly 52 minutes, with the three-minute reduction taken from the second act. The memo is currently still attached to my review queue rather than the delivery folder, so it hasn't been visible to the rest of you. This means our current 55-minute picture does not meet the delivery spec.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a credit-block issue on the business affairs side. I checked the executed lead-performer agreement, and it requires the principal credit to be represented exactly as 'Starring | Featuring Lena Ortiz', with 'Featuring Lena Ortiz' immediately after the 'Starring' credit. The agreement was signed after the generic credit block was created, and I haven't yet updated the credit sheet. So the generic principal-credit block currently in the delivery folder does not comply with the executed agreement.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag an accessibility requirement that isn't reflected in the standard delivery checklist currently in the folder. I confirmed with the distributor's accessibility vendor that this title requires English SDH as a separate WebVTT file and audio description as a separate stereo WAV file. The vendor's confirmation came in after the standard delivery checklist was circulated, so these two required deliverables aren't listed there yet. Right now, the folder only has optional subtitle files and a stereo master, which means we're missing the required SDH WebVTT and the audio description WAV. We can't get accessibility sign-off until those are added.
